elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim..." — express "defend" duty running to Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim (i)-(iv)..."; the pre-existing 12(b) indemnity in favour of Client and its affiliates is also retained.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): claim "alleging that the Interface, any related software, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — the defined service items under this Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii): "arising out of TrueLink's breach of applicable law".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii) covers "any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure caused by TrueLink of Client Content, Credit Data or any other data of Client, its affiliates or their respective customers that is provided to, transmitted through or processed by TrueLink" — the catch-all reaches every category of Client data, so the narrow § 1(d) Credit Data definition does not cap the trigger.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "arising out of TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Client shall give TrueLink prompt written notice of any claim indemnified under this Section 12".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Client shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised 12(a) now reads only: "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content ... and (ii) any breach by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default and product-injury limbs and the Web Site hook are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i) covers third-party claims that the Interface, related software, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element ("may exclude"); no such exclusion is inserted, which does not defeat the element since the carve-out is optional and its absence is Customer-favourable.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is added, so the stated condition does not apply and the element is not violated.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specifications exclusion is added, so the element is not violated.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder for infringing Interface, software or Services.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears anywhere in the revised Section 12.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is stated; the retained § 12 cap language references Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 only and is not framed as a 3x indemnity super-cap.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted paragraph delivers all four indemnity triggers (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), an express defend duty extending to Client's affiliates, and the full notice / control-of-defence / reasonable-cooperation procedure; the revised 12(a) confines Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's own breach of law.

The data-breach limb is drafted with a catch-all ("or any other data of Client, its affiliates or their respective customers that is provided to, transmitted through or processed by TrueLink"), so the artificially narrow § 1(d) Credit Data definition (31-day-old, archived, non-combined data) does not undercut the trigger.
Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, which is the claimed target.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise paragraph tracking only the checklist elements, the deletions in 12(a) are exactly those required to narrow Customer's indemnity to content and breach of law, the favourable existing 12(b) TrueLink indemnity and the § 12 cap survive untouched, and no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, Client Content and Credit Data all remain defined), no cross-reference dangles, and the retained 12(b) breach-of-Agreement indemnity is additive rather than contradictory to the new paragraph.

Optional drafting note (not a defect against the checklist): TrueLink is given control of settlement without a Client-consent proviso for settlements imposing liability or admissions on Client; if raised in negotiation, that could be tightened without affecting element coverage.
